C1.description: Two and only two tubular structures are visible entering the gallbladder.

items.text: The gallbladder neck (infundibulum) region is clearly visible and in-frame.
There are exactly two tubular attachment tracks entering the gallbladder wall.
The two tubular structures are visually distinguishable from each other at the gallbladder entry.
The gallbladder entry site is sufficiently exposed that no additional tubular structure could plausibly be hidden.
Camera angle and exposure are sufficient to confidently assess the number of tubular structures entering the gallbladder.
No instrument is present, or if present, it does not obscure the intersection between the gallbladder and the tubular structures.

C2.description: The hepatocystic triangle is cleared of fat and fibrous tissue.

items.text: The hepatocystic triangle region is clearly visible and in-frame.
Minimal fat or fibrous tissue is within the hepatocystic triangle.
Liver parenchyma is visible within the hepatocystic triangle (i.e., between the cystic duct and the liver edge), not merely beneath the gallbladder.
No continuous sheet of fat or fibrous tissue spans across and occludes the interior of the hepatocystic triangle.
Camera angle and exposure are sufficient to confidently assess hepatocystic triangle clearance.
No instrument is present, or if present, it does not obscure the interior of the hepatocystic triangle.

C3.description: The lower third of the gallbladder is detached from the liver bed.

items.text: The boundary between the gallbladder wall and liver at the lower third is clearly visible and in-frame.
A clearly visible separation interface indicating detachment is present between the gallbladder wall and the liver bed in the lower third.
The exposed liver bed (cystic plate) surface is visible at the detachment site of the lower third of the gallbladder.
The detachment extends across a substantial portion of the lower third, not just a focal point.
No continuous tissue bridge connects the lower third of the gallbladder to the liver bed.
Camera angle and exposure are sufficient to confidently assess gallbladder detachment from the liver bed.
No instrument is present, or if present, it does not obscure the gallbladder–liver interface.

label_type_definitions.precondition: Visibility or identifiability prerequisite for judging the criterion; not direct proof of satisfaction.
label_type_definitions.evidence: Direct visual evidence supporting or refuting criterion satisfaction.
label_type_definitions.modifier: Factors that affect confidence by influencing observability (e.g., camera angle, instrument occlusion), not the surgical state itself.
